caption:
The Browser Company is shutting down Arc. The browser stops working on Mac and Windows on December 22, 2026.
Arc Search on phones loses its AI features on November 23, and new Arc accounts are already closed.
Everyone is being moved to Dia, the company's AI-first browser, because keeping a browser secure keeps getting harder in the age of AI.

Would you switch to Dia or leave for another browser?

paragraphs.text: The Browser Company announced on Thursday, October 22, 2026, that it will sunset its Arc web browser on December 22, 2026, and direct users to Dia, its AI-first browser, according to TechCrunch. New Arc accounts could no longer be created as of the day of the announcement.

The company tied the decision to the cost of browser security. In its statement, quoted by TechCrunch, it said keeping a browser secure requires constant, dedicated work that keeps growing in the age of AI, and that Dia was built from the ground up to meet current security standards. Its engineering and security teams will now concentrate on Dia.

The shutdown happens in three steps. On October 22, account creation closed. On November 23, Arc Search on iOS and Android loses its AI features, including the Browse for Me tool, and sign-in and tab sync stop. The mobile app remains usable only as a basic local browser after that date.

On December 22, Arc stops working on Mac and Windows and Arc accounts are deactivated. TechCrunch reported that personal data will be deleted within 30 days after that, and that Arc Search will be removed from the Google Play Store.

The Browser Company says Dia can import passwords, bookmarks, extensions and browsing history from Arc. Several of Arc's signature features have equivalents: Spaces become Profiles, vertical tabs are available as an optional sidebar, and Folders become Pinned Tab Groups. According to the reports, Arc's features stay free in Dia and the AI functions are optional.

Geo News reported that Dia is free on Apple Silicon Macs and Windows 11 PCs. The company also claims Dia already performs better than Arc on speed, stability and security tests, according to TechCrunch.
Why Arc will not be open-sourced

Reaction on social media was largely disappointed, and many users asked the company to release Arc as open source, TechCrunch reported. Arc runs on the Arc Development Kit, a proprietary internal toolkit that also powers Dia. Chief executive Josh Miller has said that open-sourcing Arc would require releasing that toolkit, which he described as core to the company's value.

Active feature development on Arc had already stopped in 2025, although the company continued to maintain the browser while it built Dia. Miller's team had earlier acknowledged that Arc's complexity, which it called a novelty tax, limited mainstream adoption. Atlassian acquired The Browser Company for $610 million in 2025.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the decision shows how AI features are reshaping browser economics. A small team that once ran two browsers is consolidating on the one built around AI, and it is presenting security as the main constraint. For Arc's loyal users, the practical cost is a forced migration within two months, with some familiar workflows renamed rather than removed.
The next date to watch is November 23, when Arc Search loses its AI features and syncing, which will show how many mobile users follow the company to Dia.
